t: This is Downing Street, a gated cul-de-sac off Whitehall, about 200 metres long. It holds the official homes and offices of the Prime Minister and the Chancellor of the Exchequer. Sir George Downing developed it in the 1680s and gave it his name. He served under the Commonwealth and then Charles II, and helped bring about the acquisition of New York from the Dutch in 1665. Sir Henry Campbell-Bannerman, Prime Minister from 1905 to 1908, died here. The fashion figure Beau Brummell was born here.
